extracted.intended_audience: NIH extramural applicants, grantee organization staff, and federal/agency users who use eRA Commons (PIs, SOs, AOs, AAs, ASSTs, BOs, FCOI administrators)
extracted.subtask_description: Procedural and policy instructions for creating and managing eRA Commons accounts, preparing and submitting grant-related documents (e.g., RPPRs, RAMs, reference letters), using modules (FCOI, xTRACT), and performing post-award amendments within the NIH eRA Commons system.

rubrics_metrics.name: Attachment file format and size
rubrics_metrics.description: All attachments should be submitted in PDF format with a maximum size of 6MB.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This is a general requirement across Commons. Ensure PDFs are not password-protected (see reference letter rules) and verify file size before upload to avoid submission errors.

rubrics_metrics.name: Reference letter formatting and upload constraints
rubrics_metrics.description: Letters of reference must be no longer than 2 pages and in the PDF format. The PDF cannot be password-protected and should not be fillable.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: For fellowship and career development applications, a separate reference letter form is no longer required; a letter on institutional letterhead is acceptable. After submission both the referee and candidate receive confirmation emails; the candidate cannot view the submitted letter. To submit a corrected letter, resubmit with the previous Reference Letter Confirmation number. Follow the Submit Reference Letter screen steps and attach the PDF before clicking Submit.

rubrics_metrics.name: Reference letter submission prerequisites
rubrics_metrics.description: To submit a reference letter the candidate must have a Commons account and hold the PI role; otherwise submission will fail (error: Commons User ID of Applicant entered is invalid).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The candidate's SO or Accounts Administrator must assign the PI role if missing. The referee must be provided the applicant’s PI Commons User ID, the PI's last name as it appears in Commons, the FOA number, FOA opening date and application submission deadline.

rubrics_metrics.name: Username and password rules / login security
rubrics_metrics.description: Commons requires a unique user ID (6 to 20 characters). Passwords display as asterisks and the system locks users out after three unsuccessful login attempts.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use the Forgot Password/Unlock Account link to reset and obtain a temporary password, then change to a password of your choosing. Temporary or expired passwords must be changed before linking federated accounts. For full password requirements refer to the NIH eRA Password Policy (link provided in guide).

rubrics_metrics.name: Account lockout and recovery
rubrics_metrics.description: Accounts are locked after multiple unsuccessful login attempts and can be reset via the Forgot Password/Unlock Account process which generates a temporary password.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: After receiving a temporary password, immediately change it to one of your choosing. If federated account linking or other issues persist, contact the eRA Service Desk.

rubrics_metrics.name: Session expiration / logout practice
rubrics_metrics.description: Work sessions expire after 45 minutes of inactivity; users should save changes and log out when finished.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Log out via the Logout link in the upper right corner before closing the browser to avoid session timeouts or data loss.

rubrics_metrics.name: Final RPPR closeout timing and content differences
rubrics_metrics.description: The Final Research Performance Progress Report (Final RPPR) must be submitted no later than 120 days from the project end date and replaces the Final Progress Report (FPR) for closeout.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Final RPPR uses section D.1 for 'Participants', does not use sections F (Changes) or H (Budget), and adds a new Section I (Outcomes) that will be made publicly available. Deadlines remain the same; small businesses may have a delayed availability date. The Signing Official (SO) may delegate submission of the Final RPPR or Interim-RPPR to a PD/PI.

rubrics_metrics.name: SO delegation of Final RPPR submission
rubrics_metrics.description: NIH maintains the business rule allowing the Signing Official (SO) to delegate the submission of the Final RPPR or Interim-RPPR to a Program Director/Principal Investigator (PD/PI).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Ensure proper delegations are set in Commons so the PD/PI can access the submission functionality when delegated by the SO.

rubrics_metrics.name: ORCID linking procedure
rubrics_metrics.description: ORCID IDs must be added/linked in NCBI (MyNCBI); once linked there, the update propagates to the Commons profile.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If you do not have an ORCID, create one at orcid.org. Follow NCBI/NCBI instructions to link; Commons does not manage ORCID directly.

rubrics_metrics.name: Maintain single Commons account when changing institutions
rubrics_metrics.description: PIs moving institutions should maintain a single Commons account and have the SO at the new institution affiliate that existing Commons account with the new organization; the SO at the old institution should disaffiliate if desired.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Benefits include consolidated grant record history, proper recording of reviewer service, accurate NIH records, and better handling of Early Stage Investigator eligibility. If you have multiple Commons accounts, contact the eRA Service Desk to have them merged. Note: system users with the SO role must create a new account at the new institution.

rubrics_metrics.name: Federated (institution/organization) sign-in linking constraints
rubrics_metrics.description: When linking a federated organization credential to a Commons account, you cannot use a system-assigned temporary password, an expired password, or a locked account; these must be changed/unlocked first.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If account linking fails, read on-screen messages and tips; change/reset your Commons password first if needed. For other linking issues contact the eRA Service Desk. During the pilot some Commons features may be limited for federated logins—use your eRA User ID/password if you encounter feature access problems.

rubrics_metrics.name: Role-based access and responsibilities
rubrics_metrics.description: Commons assigns specific roles (e.g., Account Administrator (AA), Administrative Official (AO), Assistant (ASST), Business Official (BO), Signing Official (SO), Program Director/Principal Investigator (PI), FCOI roles) and the modules and actions a user can access depend on those roles.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Examples: SO typically completes FCOI reporting unless delegated; federal staff must also have a Commons role to log in; modules visible/accessibility depend on role and affiliated institution. Consult the user guide sections detailing each role for precise capabilities.

rubrics_metrics.name: FCOI module requirement and capabilities
rubrics_metrics.description: The Financial Conflict of Interest (FCOI) module is mandatory for all institutions and allows initiation/preparation/submission of FCOI reports and supporting documents, annual reports, revisions, mitigation reports, notifications, search/view of submitted reports, audit/history access, and assignment of FCOI access to other users.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Typically the institution's Signing Official (SO) completes FCOI reporting unless the SO delegates the FCOI role (FCOI_ASST, FCOI_View) to others. Refer to Office of Extramural Research FCOI policies for regulatory requirements (42 CFR Part 50 Subpart F).

rubrics_metrics.name: Non-Research amendment types and initiation workflow
rubrics_metrics.description: When initiating post-award non-research amendment applications, users choose amendment types such as Budget Revision, Carryover Request, Change in Scope, Key Personnel, Merger/Transfer/etc., No-Cost Extension, and Organization Change.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Clicking an amendment option opens the ASSIST module with required forms. PI users see only grants on which they are PI; a checkbox allows including expired grants. Ensure SAM registration expiration date is after submission date before initiating an amendment.

rubrics_metrics.name: Manage/View Amendments search and view behavior
rubrics_metrics.description: PIs and SOs use the Manage Post Award Amendments search to locate eligible grants; results can be sorted; if an amendment exists for a grant a View button is shown in addition to Initiate.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: SOs can run institution-wide searches and use filters. View opens amendment statuses; Action(s) menu offers View Prior RAM (consolidated PDF) or Edit RAM where allowed. Back to Search and Initiate functions available on Amendments view screens.

rubrics_metrics.name: Request for Additional Materials (RAM) submission rules
rubrics_metrics.description: RAMs allow upload of up to 10 documents (individual documents may not exceed 6MB). The RAM includes a required free-form justification field and provides Cancel, View, Save, and Submit actions.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: There can be only one active (non-submitted) RAM at a time for edits; once submitted no further changes can be made to that RAM and files/justification will be appended to the final summary PDF. Both PI and SO can edit/save RAMs prior to submission. The system provides an audit trail of who uploaded documents and sends an email notification to the Government Project Officer (GPO), Grant Technical Assistant (GTA), and Grants Management Specialist (GMS) upon submission. Verify uploaded documents before submitting; the agency receives a single combined PDF.

rubrics_metrics.name: RAM document handling and audit trail
rubrics_metrics.description: The system consolidates uploaded RAM documents into one PDF presented to the agency and maintains an audit trail of who uploaded each document.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Check the consolidated list after upload (latest on top). There is no limit to the number of RAMs that can be submitted over time, but only one may be active for editing at a time.

rubrics_metrics.name: xTRACT training table rules
rubrics_metrics.description: xTRACT is a tool for creating training tables that must be attached to and submitted with the appropriate progress report or application; xTRACT itself has no Submit feature.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: xTRACT can pre-populate data from xTrain (trainee names, characteristics, institutions, grant numbers, subsequent awards) and also allows manual entry; manually entered data is stored in xTRAIN for reuse. Use xTRACT Online Help and guide notes for specifics.

rubrics_metrics.name: Reference letter correction procedure
rubrics_metrics.description: To submit a corrected reference letter, resubmit via the Submit Reference Letter screen and enter the Reference Letter Confirmation number from the previous submission.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Attach the corrected PDF and submit; both referee and candidate will receive a confirmation email indicating receipt.

rubrics_metrics.name: Grant number composition requirements
rubrics_metrics.description: A complete NIH grant number is composed of parts including Application Type, Activity Code, Institute/Center Code, Serial Number, Support Year, and optional Suffix Code.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When referencing or searching by grant number ensure each component is accurate (e.g., '1 R01 CA 123456-01A1'). See Grants & Funding site for activity code and program-type details.
